channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone's vice presidency has never produced a president
item.description: Analyst Foday M. Daboh argues that the office is often used to balance factions rather than to groom successors, leaving holders without a clear path to power.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning fuels deforestation
item.description: The practice, driven by limited access to electricity and clean cooking, leads to environmental degradation and threatens food security.

item.title: Eswatini U-23 team beats Algeria
item.description: The national Under-23 football team's victory over Algeria has boosted national pride after a series of poor senior team performances.

item.title: Gunmen demand N500m for abducted FUNAAB graduate, three others
item.description: Four people, including a recent university graduate, were taken from a farm in Ogun State on Tuesday night.

item.title: Tanzania plans solar power and clean cooking for 1.4 million poor households
item.description: The Light to Learn initiative, presented at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, is aimed especially at girls whose homework is squeezed out by household chores.

item.title: Namibia traders excluded from FMD relief
item.description: Informal meat vendors in Windhoek say government aid for Foot-and-Mouth Disease bypasses them, leaving them without cashflow.

item.title: Liberia charges seven people over attack on police officer in Sinkor
item.description: Officer Sedeke K. Kammara reportedly lost use of an eye and had his radio, cap and US$150 taken during the assault

item.title: Chad court keeps two men in custody over alleged Boko Haram links
item.description: The Tribunal de grande instance in N'Djamena ordered both suspects held while investigators pursue further inquiries into their alleged ties to the group.

item.title: Central African opposition gives government 14 days to meet demands
item.description: The BRDC coalition, which includes the former prime minister Martin Ziguélé, is demanding the release of detainees and lower fuel prices.

item.title: Senegal parents learn to manage child diabetes
item.description: An association organized a conference in Dakar to support parents of children with diabetes, aiming for better care and integration.

item.title: University of Lomé launches 2026-2027 doctoral year
item.description: The ceremony brought together researchers, doctoral students and partner universities, including Kara, Datcha and Winneba in Ghana, around the theme of interdisciplinarity.

item.title: Ghana Stock Exchange assesses blockchain to modernise capital market
item.description: The exchange is weighing digital assets and distributed ledger systems to improve trading, ownership records and settlement.

item.title: Burundi city disrupted by blaring advertisements
item.description: Loud, repetitive advertising panels in Gitega are causing economic losses and health concerns for residents and businesses.

item.title: Angola seeks tourism investment at BITUR 2026 fair in Luanda
item.description: The International Stock Exchange of Tourism of Angola, held in Luanda, will bring operators, investors and partners together to build business deals.

item.title: Mkaka dares accusers to produce evidence of corruption
item.description: Former Malawi Congress Party Secretary General Eisenhower Mkaka says he will open his assets to anti-corruption investigators if they have reasonable grounds to suspect wrongdoing.

item.title: Tatunane band pioneered global Tanzanian music
item.description: The 1980s band fused American and Tanzanian sounds, winning international awards but gaining little local traction.

item.title: Tanzania, Nordic nations discuss AI in health
item.description: Tanzania and Nordic countries will collaborate with Muhimbili University to improve health systems using AI technology.

item.title: Sovereign fund watchdog says it was shut out of key policy work
item.description: Mozambique's Supervisory Committee of the Sovereign Fund says the Finance Ministry was slow to share information and left it out of drafting the Investment Policy.

item.title: Kenya seeks safeguards for youth seeking jobs in Germany
item.description: Nairobi forum highlights need for ethical recruitment and worker protection amid growing labour mobility.

item.title: Benoni Urey named Liberia's seat on ECOWAS Business Council
item.description: The advisory body, chaired by Aliko Dangote, is meant to give the private sector a direct line to West Africa's presidents.

item.title: Togo opens 2026 national Vététré championship with 13 clubs
item.description: 13 clubs split across three zones will contest a traditional sport whose final round is set for 13 December.

item.title: Malawi health workers threaten walkout
item.description: A coalition of health workers has given the government a 14-day ultimatum to address critical shortages and staffing issues.

item.title: Jordan's Princess Sarah Zeid visits Mozambique's Cabo Delgado
item.description: UN official assesses health and well-being of mothers and children affected by crisis in northern province.

item.title: Gunmen kill two in ambush on SPLM delegates in Mundri
item.description: Gunmen attacked a vehicle carrying SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri East County, killing a former journalist and a former teacher.

item.title: Four UNN students die at off-campus party
item.description: A survivor recounts losing consciousness after consuming alcohol at a gathering in Nsukka, Enugu State.

item.title: Nimba community opens new seven-classroom school
item.description: Residents of Yokopa in Nimba County celebrate the opening of a new school building funded by ArcelorMittal Liberia's Social Development Fund.

item.title: Central bank asks public to take part in emigration and currency survey
item.description: The Central Bank of Sao Tome and Principe is collecting views on emigration, the foreign exchange market and inflation expectations until November 22.

item.title: Kenya and Saudi Arabia agree three-month pilot to review domestic worker recruitment fees
item.description: The pilot will test voluntary recruitment fees based on market cost, following a technical annex signed in Riyadh.

item.title: College principal butchered in bedroom attack
item.description: Unknown assailants broke into Gerishom Wafula Manase's home in Kakamega County and killed him with crude weapons.

item.title: Ignite Namibia unveils granite pencil and local bottled water
item.description: Both products were commissioned by Ignite Namibia and launched at a breakfast event in Windhoek on Wednesday.

item.title: Court hears lawyer Essa Faal owed money in D58.9m fraud case
item.description: GACH Global Trading Company Limited is suing two former officials over funds allegedly obtained through a fraudulent petroleum supply deal.

item.title: Botswana adds intelligence vetting for Special Economic Zone investors
item.description: SEZA Botswana has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Directorate of Intelligence and Security to screen applicants before licences are issued.

item.title: Clashes at Balato leave 10 dead and 13 injured in Guinea
item.description: The government says the violence broke out during a patrol enforcing a ban on illegal gold panning in the Siguiri region.

item.title: Gambia hosts regional maritime ministers in Banjul
item.description: Ministers and experts from West and Central Africa will weigh a proposed regional maritime bank and the transformation of MOWCA into a continental body.

item.title: Uganda ranks 23rd of 56 Commonwealth countries on youth AI readiness
item.description: A Commonwealth study says Uganda scores 47.0 out of 100, below its readiness benchmark of 53, and that AI could add US$899 million to its GDP over a decade.

item.title: Nigeria faces power cuts over N639bn unpaid gas debt
item.description: Unpaid gas debts totaling N639 billion threaten Nigeria's electricity supply, impacting power generation.

item.title: Erdoğan and Tshisekedi meet in Antalya, Turkey reaffirms DR Congo's territorial integrity
item.description: Turkey's president backed the Democratic Republic of Congo's territorial integrity at a meeting with President Félix Tshisekedi on the sidelines of the COP31 climate conference.

item.title: RSF arrests Rizeigat members after deadly tribal clashes in East Darfur
item.description: Seven people died and six were injured after a Rizeigat attack on Um Dirab, an area inhabited by the Habbaniya tribe.

item.title: Rwandan forces capture six suspected insurgents in Pangane village
item.description: The suspects were detained while buying food for insurgents in a village that has served as a supply point for the group.

item.title: Old Mutual commits N$300 000 to Kunene food security
item.description: The funding supports gardening infrastructure, equipment, and training through the Green Futures Garden Project.

item.title: South Sudan ministry demands 70% local staff on donor-funded projects
item.description: The agriculture ministry wants UN agencies such as FAO and UNOPS to fill most project jobs with South Sudanese graduates, leaving 30 percent for foreigners.

item.title: Chapo courts Turkish investors for Mozambique gas, power and corridor projects
item.description: The president told business leaders in Antalya that the country has recently carried out public sector reforms that make it a favourable place to raise capital.

item.title: China offers Liberia mining investment and US$3 million in rice aid
item.description: Beijing proposes that African countries own their mineral resources, while Liberian cocoa producers are set to gain access to the Chinese market from December 15, 2026.

item.title: Water runs short at Kosti displacement camp as fuel dries up
item.description: Thousands of displaced families at the Goz Al-Salam camp are going without steady drinking water as power and diesel supplies falter.

item.title: Port-Louis municipality threatens street vendors with sanctions
item.description: The city council warns of severe penalties for illegal occupation of public spaces and drains ahead of the festive season.

item.title: Tunisia to overhaul military service law with higher pay and training
item.description: Defence Minister Khaled Sehili says a new draft law to replace the 2004 national service law is complete and aims to make the service more attractive and flexible.

item.title: Herminie inspects La Digue school and seawall works on official visit
item.description: The president is on the island for his second official visit since taking office, reviewing projects across three sites.

item.title: Comoros shows its pilgrim services at Hajj exhibition in Jeddah
item.description: The national Hajj agency is presenting its support for pilgrims at a Saudi congress that brings together more than 520 organisations from over 150 countries.

item.title: Madagascar's National Assembly vice-president denies plot to oust leadership
item.description: Fanomezantsoa Andrianjanahary says no move to remove the permanent bureau is under way, and the 2027 finance bill is being examined.

item.title: Cameroon ships 17 tons of coffee to China duty-free
item.description: A first shipment of 17 metric tons of Cameroonian coffee is reportedly on its way to China under a zero-tariff deal that took effect on May 1, 2026.

item.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair opens at Accra Mall
item.description: The three-day exhibition, running November 13 to 15, lets Ghanaian firms sell directly to shoppers under one roof.

item.title: Africa experts push digital tech against fake seeds
item.description: African agricultural experts met in Dar es Salaam to discuss using digital technology and biotechnology to improve seed quality and food security.

item.title: Zambia to take over K1.7 billion NHIMA debt owed to hospitals
item.description: Health Minister Roma Chilengi announced Thursday that Cabinet has also approved a package of reforms to overhaul how the National Health Insurance Management Authority is funded.

item.title: Court fines three men K800,000 each over 670 litres of petrol
item.description: The fuel has been forfeited to the government after the men were found with it in Dwangwa, Nkhotakota District.

item.title: Farm attack survivor Donovan Marx leaves hospital
item.description: Donovan Marx, who was shot, stabbed, and had both ears cut off, was discharged from Mediclinic Potchefstroom on Thursday, 12 November.

item.title: Tunisia faces cooler temperatures and rain
item.description: Winds will be strong near the northern coast and in the south, with local sandstorms possible.

item.title: 170 teachers complete training in Malagasy language and mathematics
item.description: The Ministry of National Education awarded certificates to 170 teachers who finished training in Malagasy language and mathematics.

item.title: Musokotwane names mining, farming, tourism and energy as jobs engines
item.description: Zambia's finance minister says growth in four key sectors is needed before ordinary households can afford home loans.

item.title: Zambia launches youth agriculture program
item.description: The Pro-Agro Youth Programme aims to boost agricultural productivity and rural economies.

item.title: Police in Nchelenge arrest fisherman over Lake Mweru killing
item.description: Police say the 36-year-old suspect allegedly killed his 58-year-old fellow fisherman, Abraham Kanyembo, on Lake Mweru in Luapula Province.

item.title: Ghana aims for 100% local cocoa processing by 2030
item.description: Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson urged international buyers to add value in Ghana, as the government plans to process all cocoa domestically.

item.title: Mali detains four pro-democracy activists
item.description: Four activists, previously held illegally for six months, have been formally charged and imprisoned.

item.title: Warren Caddy's goal is cancelled out as Madagascar draws 1-1 with Guinea-Bissau
item.description: Madagascar remain on two points from three CAN 2027 qualifiers after a late equaliser in Meknès on Thursday.

item.title: Madagascar and Russia to build farm school
item.description: An agreement signed in Moscow will also see Russian agricultural technology transferred to Madagascar.

item.title: Eswatini names Cebisile Ngwenya to lead co-operatives department
item.description: The magistrate and former High Court official replaces the late Russell Nxumalo, who died in October 2025, as the sector faces financial and governance strain.

item.title: Police probe death of missing guard found in Mfabantfu forest
item.description: Preliminary findings suggest the 40-year-old from Ekudzeni may have swallowed a poisonous substance, but the cause of death is not yet confirmed.

item.title: BoG defends new GH¢50 note portrait
item.description: Bank of Ghana board member Beatrice Annan says the image of flag designer Theodosia Okoh was adapted from authentic photos for banknote production.

item.title: Ethiopian army takes control of Tigray capital Mekelle
item.description: Hundreds of people are reported dead after the renewed fighting, which began in late September.

item.title: Gambia urged to sign fisheries transparency deal
item.description: Stakeholders want a Memorandum of Understanding with the Fisheries Transparency Initiative to improve marine surveillance and data collection.

item.title: Ghana army disputes claims it abandoned stampede victim, cites GH¢143,800 support
item.description: The military says it has spent about GH¢143,800 on Sandra's care, including GH¢85,000 in KATH bills and GH¢28,800 for her eight-month stay at the 37 Military Hospital in Accra.

item.title: Chad police inspect stations after child street operations
item.description: Police chief Tougoud Digo Maïdé visited three N'Djamena police stations on November 12, 2026, following recent operations to control and apprehend children on the streets.

item.title: Mauritania's national team arrives in Ouagadougou for Africa Cup of Nations qualifier
item.description: The Mourabitounes landed early on Thursday and face Burkina Faso in the third round of qualifying for the 2027 tournament, with a return match in Nouakchott next Tuesday.

item.title: Mauritanian prosecutors seek charges against 28 in 'bloggers from abroad' case
item.description: Charges are sought against 28 people, with arrest warrants requested for seven, over alleged criminal organisation, false information and terrorism financing.

item.title: Moroccan MPs push marketing reform to bring down food prices
item.description: Lawmakers say some produce doubles or triples in price after leaving wholesale markets, with losses on tomatoes and potatoes reaching around 30%.

item.title: Burundi police hold 21 residents over fertiliser protest
item.description: At least 21 people, including four women and three infants, remain in custody after a dispute over fertiliser distribution in Gitega province.

item.title: Adjohoun adopts first budget under Mayor Hounkanrin
item.description: The Benin commune of Adjohoun will operate with a 1.92 billion FCFA budget for 2027.

item.title: Burundi arrests prison director and two officials over businessman's privileges
item.description: The three Mpimba prison officials are held by the National Intelligence Service (SNR), accused of granting special treatment to a businessman linked to trade in M23-controlled.

item.title: Nigeria hands Port Harcourt airport to private firm for 30 years
item.description: Port Harcourt Airport Company Ltd. will run the Rivers State airport under a concession agreement signed by the Federal Government.

item.title: Benin signs AI deal with China
item.description: The country becomes the first pilot nation for an AI initiative supported by UNESCO.

item.title: Super Sécurité professionalises private security in Guinea
item.description: The Conakry-based firm has secured over 100 clients and operates at more than 150 sites nationwide.

item.title: Senegal beats Sudan 4-1 in CAN qualifier
item.description: The Lions secured a dominant second-half performance to take the lead in Group J.

item.title: Ivory Coast beats Gambia 2-1 in CAN 2027 qualifier in Bouaké
item.description: The Elephants move level on six points with Gambia at the top of Group C, with a return leg set for Bakau on Tuesday, 17 November.

item.title: Sao Tome president rejects MLSTP government proposal
item.description: President Carlos Vila Nova has asked the second-placed ADI party to form a government after the MLSTP failed to prove parliamentary support.

item.title: Chad launches free cataract surgery drive for 700 people in Mongo
item.description: Patients in Guéra province will receive free operations, medicines and care under a national blindness programme.

item.title: Senegal beats Sudan 4-1 in AFCON qualifier
item.description: Boulaye Dia and Ibrahima Mbaye scored second-half goals as Senegal dominated Sudan.

item.title: Mauritania refers 24 to terrorism investigation team
item.description: Prosecutors in Nouakchott West have accused 24 individuals of crimes including conspiracy against state security and money laundering.

item.title: Rwanda seeks $3bn in climate finance for electricity and urban resilience
item.description: At COP31 in Türkiye, the government presented an estimated US$3.05 billion in investment needs for its electricity ambitions, including US$1.3 billion for grid infrastructure.

item.title: Morocco cuts self-employed tax rate
item.description: The government proposes lowering the tax rate for self-employed workers from 30% to 20% while introducing measures to prevent employer abuse.

item.title: Algeria warns of climate change impact at COP31
item.description: President Tebboune highlighted desertification, drought, and wildfires as major threats to Algeria's water and food security.

item.title: Tunisia marks 70 years with UN
item.description: Tunisia reaffirms commitment to UN principles and seeks reform to end double standards.

item.title: Djibouti puts its connectivity figures before the ITU in Qatar
item.description: Around 70% of the population now uses the internet, and 350 kilometres of fibre are being laid towards the north of the country.

item.title: World Bank prepares $760 million more for Niger's energy, farming and water
item.description: The funding is added to more than $4 billion the World Bank already has committed in Niger, and is meant to support larger projects over the next five years.

item.title: Ivory Coast inaugurates Koné gold mine
item.description: The new mine, built in under two years, is now the largest in the country and one of Africa's most significant.

item.title: DR Congo beats Sierra Leone 3-1 in Kinshasa in CAN 2027 qualifier
item.description: Yoane Wissa scored in the fourth minute as the Leopards kept up pressure on the Leone Stars at the Martyrs stadium.

item.title: Cellcom Guinée workers start indefinite strike
item.description: Union members refuse to work, even without minimum service, over planned technical leave for 45 employees.

item.title: Tunisian police dismantle drug ring in Tunis, arrest three suspects
item.description: Investigators also seized a quantity of narcotics and cash from the illegal trade, officials said.

item.title: Cameroon seeks German dairy technology
item.description: The nation aims to boost milk production and cut import costs with German expertise.

item.title: UNFPA and Iceland fund fistula surgeries in Makeni and Bo
item.description: About 10 women have already been operated on at Makeni Regional Hospital, and Bo Government Hospital is next in line for 10 to 15 more.

item.title: Benin beats Central African Republic 4-1 to top Group F
item.description: Benin moved to the top of Group F in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers after a 4-1 win in Abidjan on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

item.title: Pagou names Cameroon lineup without Baleba, with Angel Yondjo Matah starting
item.description: Cameroon's coach David Pagou picked his starting 11 for the qualifier against Namibia at Japoma Stadium in Douala.
